question: What do GA's per-instrument voicing counts and cross-instrument consistency metric actually measure?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
hypothesis: Separating corpus-size bars from the shared-set consistency result may prevent readers from interpreting a set-level agreement check as per-instrument naming accuracy.
evidence: GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924: state/quality/voicing-analysis/2026-07-23.json reports 297910 guitar, 7795 bass, 7342 ukulele, 313047 total, and 793/793 shared sets consistent.
The same commit: Demos/VoicingAnalysisAudit/Program.cs records the first canonical name per instrument and pitch-class mask, then compares masks observed on at least two instruments.
The global zero null/unknown counts imply zero in each instrument cohort, but the snapshot has no independently reviewed musical-correctness labels or pairwise breakdown for the shared-set metric.
Research duration was not instrumented; duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
